title: 3D Seismic Fault Instance Segmentation for Subsurface Structural Modeling via Consensus Relation Supervision
content: Seismic interpretation for three-dimensional (3D) subsurface structural modeling requires detected fault samples to be assigned to individual faults for inspection and surface construction. Intersections and fragmented observations make these assignments difficult, and automatic geometric partitions can contain incorrect merges and splits. We propose Consensus Relation Supervision (CRS) for 3D seismic fault instance segmentation using two uncorrected geometric partitions. Spatial overlap matching extracts strict consensus cores, whose same-fault and different-fault sample pairs provide supervision independent of numerical instance identifiers. A 3D-UNet3+ network learns instance embeddings and auxiliary separation cues from binary fault volumes. Point-pair training combines local and long-range relations, with local sampling prioritizing crossing negatives and positives at weak connections. The composite objective combines a balanced soft-target relation loss with hard-positive consistency, crossing-negative separation, and auxiliary boundary supervision. At inference, learned relations guide graph grouping and label propagation, followed by geometric association of compatible fragments. Manually revised instance labels are reserved for validation, parameter selection, and evaluation. Synthetic comparisons support improved instance grouping with the selected relation targets, and qualitative applications to F3D and A2 show fault-instance organization on field data. By learning association and separation from noisy automatic interpretations, CRS produces sample groups for inspecting individual faults and constructing their surfaces, providing an instance representation for subsequent 3D subsurface structural modeling.
